value: This study investigated the frequency, circumstances, and attitudes towards placebo use in clinical practice among healthcare professionals in the Jerusalem area. A retrospective questionnaire was administered to 89 physicians and nurses from two large hospitals and various community clinics. Results indicated that 60% of respondents used placebos, with 62% of users administering them monthly or more. A significant majority (68%) informed patients they were receiving actual medication, and 94% reported finding placebos generally or occasionally effective across a wide range of conditions and for diagnostic purposes. Only 5% of respondents believed placebo use should be entirely prohibited. The study concludes that placebo use is widespread in clinical practice, suggesting that, when used judiciously, placebos might hold a legitimate therapeutic role, and emphasizes the urgent need for broader recognition and debate regarding its implications.
